q: Our carbon footprint jumped after we added supplier emissions. Did we get worse?
title: Footprint jumped after adding Scope 3
short: No. You counted more of what was always there. Scope 3 is usually the largest part of a manufacturer's footprint, so adding it raises the total even if nothing changed on site. Compare like with like: Scope 1 and 2 against last year, and restate last year with Scope 3 if you want a trend.
audience: Companies reporting Scope 3 for the first time

ul: Keep Scope 1 and 2 as a separate line with last year beside it.
Show Scope 3 as a new line, with a note on which categories are included.
If you restate the earlier year, say so and say why.

p: Buyers expect Scope 3 to be large. A clear note that the increase comes from wider coverage reads as better reporting, not worse performance.

senseible: Senseible reads supplier invoices into dated records with the quantity, unit and factor on each line, and marks lines without a usable quantity as needing data instead of guessing.

sources.label: GHG Protocol Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Standard
